## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-anonymized; "Reviewer interacts with: Co-editors"; "Review information published: None" (guidelines copy 2025-05-28, https://web.archive.org/web/20250528143554/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/crx). Manuscripts must be fully anonymized, with identifying information moved to a separate title page that is not sent to reviewers |
| **Process** | An initial evaluation first: manuscripts that do not follow the guidelines are returned for amendment and may be desk rejected if out of scope or unsuitable. Two independent reviews are required before a Revise or Accept decision; reviewers are assigned by the journal and author-suggested reviewers are not accepted; reviewers send recommendations to the co-editors, who make the final decision (same page). The journal uses editorial-board and editorial-review-board members as reviewers, at most one per manuscript from that pool before inviting others (same page) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No transfer statement found in the guidelines copy |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | No: "Review information published: None" (guidelines copy 2025-05-28) |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | SciRev: 3.0 rounds on average (1 review; https://scirev.org/journal/communication-research/). The journal itself states no figure |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Reviewers give comments to authors and recommendations to the co-editors, who decide (guidelines copy 2025-05-28). Reviewers' names stay withheld by default, though a reviewer may choose to reveal theirs |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Publisher-level only. The live guidelines (read in a real browser 2026-11-24) say AI chatbots such as ChatGPT should not be listed as authors and point to Sage's policy on use of ChatGPT and generative AI tools; the top of the page also says Sage's ethics policies cover disclosure of AI use and list prohibited uses. The journal adds no wording of its own |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate: use is allowed with disclosure. Sage's policy (copy 2024-12-13) says disclosed use will not by itself cause rejection, but an editor who finds inappropriate undisclosed use may reject at any point in the process |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with mandatory disclosure; same rubric as other AI-researched entries) |
| **Summary** | Per the Sage policy page: use of AI tools that generate references, text, images or other content must be disclosed; authors name the model and the purpose in the Methods or Acknowledgements; authors verify accuracy and citations, and cite original sources rather than the AI tool; AI cannot be an author; a submission mainly or partly AI-generated must be disclosed at submission |
| **Source URL** | https://web.archive.org/web/20241213223927/https://us.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/chatgpt-and-generative-ai (publisher policy); https://web.archive.org/web/20250528143554/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/crx (journal guidelines) |

### Preprint Policy

> Journal guidelines plus Sage's author archiving policy. Sources: guidelines copy 2025-05-28 and https://web.archive.org/web/20250706191632/https://us.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/journal-author-archiving-policies-and-re-use (snapshot 2025-07-06).

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes | The guidelines say the journal will consider manuscripts posted on preprint servers (the key information box also reads "Accepts preprints? Yes"); authors enter the preprint DOI at submission and are advised to tell the editorial office |
| Under review | Restricted | The guidelines say not to post an updated version on a preprint server while the manuscript is under peer review |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes | Sage's policy lets authors share the Original Submission or Accepted Manuscript at any time after acceptance, on any website, repository or social media, provided access is free and re-use terms are non-commercial and no-derivatives; an accepted preprint must link to the published version. No embargo is stated in that text. Embargo: none stated |
| Version of Record | Restricted | The Final Published PDF may not be posted on unrestricted sites without Sage's permission (same Sage page); open access articles follow their licence |

## Format

> Source for the rules below: the guidelines page, Wayback copy dated 2025-05-28 (https://web.archive.org/web/20250528143554/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/crx), with HTML-commented template text removed. The live page may differ.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Empirical articles and overview or review articles: "most of the published articles are empirical, we also consider overview/review articles" (description copy 2023-06-20, https://web.archive.org/web/20230620152516/https://journals.sagepub.com/description/crx). OpenAlex type counts for 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23: 264 articles, 17 reviews, 2 paratext (retrieved 2026-11-23). The guidelines copy lists no other article type |
| **Word limit** | The live guidelines (read in a real browser 2026-11-24, https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/crx) say manuscripts should be "no more than 45 pages, double spaced, inclusive of the abstract, main text, references, tables, and figures". The "12,800 word" wording of the 2025-05-28 Wayback copy did not turn up in a search of the live page text, so the page gives one limit, in pages. Supplementary files do not count toward the page limit |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. No statement on exceptions |
| **Abstract limit** | Unstructured abstract of no more than 150 words, and a minimum of 4 keywords listed after it |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the 45 pages. The journal follows APA reference style |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed (datasets, appendices, other files); online appendices are hosted with the article and can be marked "Online Appendix" at submission; appendices "should be used sparingly" |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Figures and tables go at the end of the manuscript file; tables editable and in APA format; figure resolution 300 dpi |
| **Style / submission format** | Word preferred, no template required; APA reference style; statistics reported per APA guidelines including standard deviations and effect sizes, a power analysis strongly recommended, confidence intervals when bootstrapping, correlation matrices as an online appendix strongly recommended; a separate title page with authors, affiliations (where the research was conducted), acknowledgements, conflict-of-interest, funding, ethics, consent and data availability statements; ORCID of the submitting author; submitted through Sage Track (guidelines copy 2025-05-28) |

### Orientation

> Counts below come from Crossref journal-article records for 2021-01 to 2026-11-23: 283 records, of which 277 (97.9%) carry an abstract; a record is counted when the pattern matches in its title or abstract; shares use the 277 as the denominator, so counts are lower bounds for the 6 records without an abstract (https://api.crossref.org/journals/0093-6502/works, cursor paging, retrieved 2026-11-23). Every regex is given in Methodological Preferences and Sensitive Topics. The first-pass tool `topic_trend_scan.py` was not used (known broken).

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Empirical designs dominate by keyword: experiment-type words in 89 of 277 abstracts (32.1%), survey-type words in 75 (27.1%); a broad conceptual/theoretical pattern matches 31 (11.2%), but it also matches empirical abstracts that name a theory. The journal says the same of itself: "most of the published articles are empirical" (description copy 2023-06-20) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Quantitative designs dominate: interview-type words appear in 10 (3.6%) and qualitative-method words in 6 (2.2%) of 277 abstracts, against the experiment and survey counts above |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | The aims say criteria "do not privilege any particular context" and the journal hopes to publish across "a wide variety of levels and units of analysis" (aims copy 2023-06-18, https://web.archive.org/web/20230618193305/https://journals.sagepub.com/aims-scope/crx); the 2023 description lists mass media, interpersonal, health, political, entertainment, advertising and persuasive communication, new technology, organizational, intercultural, group and family as areas. Board members' disciplines are not listed |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, stated in the aims: to qualify, research should be explicitly tied to some form of communication; be "theoretically driven with conclusions that inform theory"; use the most rigorous empirical methods or provide a review of a research area; and be directly linked to the most important problems and issues facing humankind (aims copy 2023-06-18, https://web.archive.org/web/20230618193305/https://journals.sagepub.com/aims-scope/crx).
- **What kind of engagement?** A theoretical contribution plus empirical rigor: the conclusions must inform theory, and the criteria "do not privilege any particular context" (same page). The guidelines add that the article must be within the journal's scope and of sufficient quality "or it will not be reviewed" (guidelines copy 2025-05-28, https://web.archive.org/web/20250528143554/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/crx).
- **Article type and length**: empirical and overview/review articles; up to 45 double-spaced pages including abstract, references, tables and figures (live guidelines 2026-11-24; the 12,800-word figure of the older copy no longer appears); unstructured abstract up to 150 words; at least 4 keywords (guidelines copy 2025-05-28).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: manuscripts not following the guidelines are returned for amendment, and out-of-scope manuscripts may be desk rejected without peer review (guidelines copy 2025-05-28). No data on how often this happens exists (SciRev: 1 review).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts: Crossref journal-article records 2021-01 to 2026-11-23, 283 records, 277 with an abstract; a hit is a match in title or abstract; share = hits / 277. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement. The aims ask for "the most rigorous empirical methods" or a review (aims copy 2023-06-18) and the description says most articles are empirical; neither names a single method, so no row is scored 4 or 5. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how reviewers judge it. All patterns are case-insensitive Python regexes; in table cells the alternation bar is written `\|`, read as `|`.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | `\b(experiment\w*\|randomi[sz]ed\|between-subjects?\|within-subjects?)\b` 89 of 277 (32.1%); title-only 15 of 283. Survey pattern `\b(surveys?\|questionnaires?\|self-report\w*\|panel (?:survey\|data\|study))\b` 75 (27.1%). Preregistration pattern `\bpre-?regist\w*` 19 (6.9%). The guidelines ask for APA-style statistics with effect sizes and recommend power analyses (guidelines copy 2025-05-28) |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | `\b(interview\w*\|semi-structured\|focus groups?)\b` 10 of 277 (3.6%); broader qualitative pattern `\b(qualitative\|thematic analysis\|ethnograph\w*\|discourse analysis\|grounded theory)\b` 6 (2.2%); title-only 2 of 283 |
| Autoethnography | 0 | `\bautoethnograph\w*` 0 of 277 abstracts and 0 titles |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | `\b(conceptual\w*\|theori[sz]\w*)\b` 31 of 277 (11.2%); the pattern also matches empirical abstracts that mention a theory, so it overstates purely theoretical work; title-only 4 of 283 |
| Mixed methods | 2 | `\bmixed[- ]methods?\b` 3 of 277 (1.1%) |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 3 | `\b(meta-analy\w*\|systematic review\w*\|meta-synthesis\|scoping review)\b` 29 of 277 (10.5%); title-only 23 of 283 (e.g. https://doi.org/10.1177/00936502221137165); the description says review articles are considered |
| Computational / digital-trace methods (added row) | 2 | `\b(computational\|machine learning\|topic model\w*\|natural language processing\|large language models?\|web tracking\|digital trace\w*)\b` 5 of 277 (1.8%); content-analysis pattern `\bcontent analys[ie]s\b` 10 (3.6%) |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages show, plus one SciRev report.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Stated and firm: "All papers reporting studies involving human participants, human data or human tissue must state that the relevant Ethics Committee or Institutional Review Board approved the study, or waived the requirement" with committee name, institution and approval number, under an "Ethical considerations" heading on the title page, even if already in the Methods; consent-to-participate and consent-for-publication statements are also required, each with "Not applicable" if not relevant (guidelines copy 2025-05-28, https://web.archive.org/web/20250528143554/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/crx) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author items exist but are a small minority: 23 of 277 Crossref records with author lists (2021-2026) have one author; 163 have three or more |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | No rule found: the title page asks for the affiliation where the research was conducted, and a note for a new institution; no independent-scholar clause (guidelines copy 2025-05-28, https://web.archive.org/web/20250528143554/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/crx) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Encouraged, not required: authors "are encouraged to" share data in a public repository and to include a data availability statement, and if data cannot be shared the statement should say why; the data availability statement itself is listed among the title page statements (guidelines copy 2025-05-28) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-anonymized: a fully anonymized manuscript, identifying information on a separate title page that reviewers do not see, no author names in the file name, headers or footers (guidelines copy 2025-05-28, https://web.archive.org/web/20250528143554/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/crx). A preprint is allowed before submission (Preprint Policy, https://web.archive.org/web/20250706191632/https://us.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/journal-author-archiving-policies-and-re-use), which would expose identity; the guidelines ask authors to tell the editorial office about a posted preprint |
| **AI use** | Disclose in the Methods or Acknowledgements, naming the model and purpose; AI cannot be an author (https://web.archive.org/web/20241213223927/https://us.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/chatgpt-and-generative-ai; guidelines copy 2025-05-28) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; no fee to submit or publish otherwise; OpenAlex lists an APC of 3900 USD (not confirmed by the Sage page); 90 of 283 recent works are hybrid open access in OpenAlex (see Open Access) |
| **Third-party submissions** | Writing or editing assistance from a third party must be stated in the Acknowledgements and the cover letter; the editor may decline submissions made by a third party instead of the authors (guidelines copy 2025-05-28) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope criteria**: the aims state that research must be explicitly tied to communication, theoretically driven with conclusions that inform theory, use the most rigorous empirical methods or be a review, and link to important problems (Framing Requirements; aims copy 2023-06-18). A manuscript with no theoretical conclusion is outside the stated criteria.
- **Length**: no more than 45 double-spaced pages including abstract, references, tables and figures (Format; live guidelines 2026-11-24).
- **Anonymisation**: double-anonymized review with a separate title page (Peer Review, Practical Concerns). A manuscript that cannot be anonymised does not meet the stated rules.
- **Ethics statement**: studies with human participants must state approval or waiver by a named ethics committee or IRB and give the approval number (Practical Concerns).
- **AI disclosure**: use of AI tools to generate content must be disclosed (AI Policy); undisclosed inappropriate use can lead to rejection at any stage per the Sage policy.
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact read.

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: no turnaround figure is published; the single SciRev review records 4.0 months for a first round and 9.0 months in total for an accepted paper (Review Cycle Time, n=1, undated).
- **Open access cost**: gold OA is paid through Sage Choice; OpenAlex lists 3900 USD, not confirmed by a Sage page (Open Access).
- **Reporting burden**: APA-style statistics with effect sizes, a recommended power analysis, confidence intervals for bootstrapping, a recommended correlation matrix online, and a title page of statements (Format, Practical Concerns).
- **Preprint**: allowed before submission, but no updated preprint version while under review (Preprint Policy), and a posted preprint exposes identity under double-anonymized review.

### Best Suited For

- Theory-testing experiments and surveys, which appear in 89 and 75 of 277 abstracts (Methodological Preferences).
- Interpersonal, political, news and health communication topics: interpersonal pattern `\b(interpersonal\|relationships?\|romantic\|couples?\|friendship\w*\|famil(?:y\|ies))\b` 99 of 277 abstracts (35.7%); political pattern `\b(politic\w*\|election\w*\|voting\|campaign\w*)\b` 77 (27.8%); news pattern `\b(news\|journalis\w*)\b` 54 (19.5%); `\bhealth\b` 24 (8.7%).
- Systematic reviews and meta-analyses linked to theory: 29 of 277 abstracts (Methodological Preferences).
- Authors working in teams: 163 of 277 records have three or more authors (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- Autoethnography and decolonial or Indigenous framing: 0 of 277 abstracts match either pattern (Methodological Preferences, Sensitive Topics). This shows absence, not rejection.
- Purely descriptive or atheoretical work, since the stated criteria require conclusions that inform theory (Framing Requirements).
- Qualitative-only studies: interview and qualitative-method words appear in 10 and 6 of 277 abstracts (Methodological Preferences); the counts show these are rare here, not that they are rejected.
- Authors needing a verified turnaround or acceptance figure: the journal publishes none and SciRev has 1 review (Review Cycle Time, Metrics).
